transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-03-29 15:00 UTC — 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO - Novacore), Marco Rinaldi (Head of ML), Priya Singh (SRE), Ethan Kim (PM)

Summary: POC focused on latency and throughput SLOs. Define TTFT vs TPOT targets (p95/p99), decide measurement plan (synthetic and replay), get customer traffic histograms, and deliver benchmark harness + pricing.

00:00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros?
00:00:10 Lena: Hi, Lena here, CTO at Novacore, we run conversational assistants and want lower latency for user interactions.
00:00:20 Marco: Marco, head of ML, I'll lead the POC from our side.
00:00:25 Priya: Priya, SRE, I'll provide traffic metrics and run bench infra.
00:00:30 Maya: Great, I'm Maya (AE) and Ravi (SE) from Redwood. Goal today is to align on success criteria — specifically TTFT and TPOT SLOs and how we'll measure them.

00:01:05 Ravi: So quick definitions to make sure we're aligned: TTFT is time to first token — captures cold-start and first-token latency; TPOT is time per token or token-steady-state throughput, we sometimes call it "t-per-token". For user-facing chat TTFT matters a lot because perceived latency is dominated by that first token.
00:01:35 Marco: Makes sense. We also care about p95 and p99 tails, because we get spikes where users abandon sessions.
00:01:45 Maya: Right. What are your current targets or expectations?
00:01:50 Ethan: From product — ideally TTFT p95 under 200ms for short prompts; p99 under 400ms. For TPOT we want p95 under 30ms per token and p99 under 60ms for typical generation lengths (~50 tokens).
00:02:10 Priya: Our peak concurrency today is around 250 concurrent requests, average around 90. But we have occasional peaks ~1k for promos. We'll upload histograms.
00:02:30 Ravi: Helpful. For the POC we usually size two profiles: "nominal" (expected steady-state 100-250 concurrency) and "peak" (~1k). We'll run synthetic and replay benchmarks. Synthetic for controlled TTFT/TPOT measurement, replay for realistic prompt distribution.
00:03:00 Maya: Let's capture concrete success criteria: suggestion — TTFT p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms; TPOT p95 < 30ms, p99 < 70ms at nominal load. At peak we can relax or show graceful degradation and fallback (e.g., smaller model or reduced tokens).
00:03:30 Marco: Those numbers are aggressive but in line with our product needs. Two clarifying q's: 1) Are these measured with cached KV? 2) How do you handle batching effects?
00:03:45 Ravi: Good q's. We'll define measurement policies: separate measurements for cold (no KV cache, container cold-start simulation) and warm (KV cache primed). Batching will be controlled — we'll test both single-request latency (minimal batching) and batched throughput modes. We'll also track batch sizes and queueing latency.
00:04:15 Priya: For our production, most requests hit warm cache ~70% of the time. Cold-starts happen on model version changes and new users.
00:04:25 Maya: We'll plan benchmark runs:
- Cold-start TTFT test: spin up fresh instances, send representative prompts, measure p50/p95/p99 TTFT.
- Warm TTFT: prime KV cache then measure.
- Steady-state TPOT test: sustained load at target concurrencies for 15-30 minutes to capture tail behavior.
- Replay test: replay a sample of real requests (customer provides logs) to validate end-to-end.

00:05:10 Marco: For measurement tooling what do you recommend?
00:05:15 Ravi: We supply a benchmark harness (wrk-based for simple runs, locust for complex flows) that includes: timestamped request traces, token-level timing where possible, Redwood trace capture for backend timing, and post-run analysis scripts to compute p95/p99 for TTFT/TPOT and per-route breakdowns.
00:05:35 Maya: We'll include example prompts and a config to reproduce our runs.

00:06:00 Lena: On targets, product is pushing for a p95 TTFT 150ms if possible for core flows. Is that feasible?
00:06:10 Ravi: Depends on model size, quantization and infra. For smaller distilled models on A100-like hardware, 150ms p95 TTFT for short prompts is often achievable with warm cache and tuned kernels. For larger models or cold starts, it's harder. We should set pragmatic targets split by model class.

00:06:40 Marco: Good — we'll pick two model families for the POC: an optimized 7B variant and a higher-quality 30B variant to compare.
00:06:50 Priya: Also need details on network overhead — we're in GCP us-west; any region considerations?
00:06:58 Maya: We'll run hosted infra in the same region where possible. If you need private deployment we can replicate tests on Dedicated nodes in your VPC, but that adds setup time.

00:07:20 Ravi: Measurement plan details:
- Metrics: TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT p50/p95/p99, throughput (RPS), tail latency, CPU/GPU utilization, GPU mem, and queueing delay.
- Test durations: short runs (1-5 minutes) for quick iterations; long runs (15-30 minutes) for steady-state.
- Concurrency sweep: run at 1/4 nominal, nominal, and peak (e.g., 50, 250, 1000).
- Sample sizes: at least 10k requests per steady-state point to get stable p99 estimates.

00:08:30 Marco: 10k sounds fine, might need ramp time to avoid artificial spikes.
00:08:35 Priya: We'll provide traffic histograms and a sample of prompts (stripped for PII).
00:08:45 Maya: On success criteria we'll agree on two tiers:
- "Pass": meets nominal SLOs (TTFT p95 < 200ms, TPOT p95 < 30ms) with acceptable resource profile.
- "Target": meets tighter product targets (TTFT p95 < 150ms, TPOT p95 < 25ms).

00:09:20 Ethan: I like tiers. Also want to define acceptance for p99 — maybe p99 within 2x p95 for pass?
00:09:30 Ravi: Reasonable. We'll report both absolute and relative tail ratios.

00:09:45 Marco: Any thoughts on caching strategy to improve TTFT?
00:09:50 Ravi: Prefix KV caching helps a lot for multi-turn sessions. Also model sharding and async prefetch for common prompts. We'll document recommendations.

00:10:20 Lena: For the POC timeline, what's realistic?
00:10:25 Maya: Proposed timeline:
- Day 0-3: NDA + POC paperwork; collect traffic histograms and prompt samples.
- Day 4-10: Redwood config + benchmark harness delivery; customer validation of samples.
- Week 2 (w/c 2026-04-06): Run first synthetic + replay benchmarks and share results.
- Week 3: Tuning (batching, quantization, routing) and rerun.

00:11:00 Priya: We can get histograms by end of week.
00:11:05 Marco: We'll confirm model choices this week.

00:11:30 Maya: Any compliance/security constraints that affect testing?
00:11:35 Priya: Data residency is us-west only, logs must be scrubbed and forwarded via secure bucket, and we need SAML SSO to access dashboards.
00:11:45 Maya: Noted — Redwood supports region constraints and SSO; we'll include security docs.

00:12:05 Ravi: On reporting: we'll produce a benchmark report with raw traces, p50/p95/p99 tables, latency histograms, token distributions, and recommended tuning steps. We'll also surface cost estimates (per-token cost at observed throughput).

00:12:35 Ethan: Cost is important. Show us cost delta for batching and for quantized model variants.
00:12:45 Ravi: We'll include that in the report.

00:13:00 Lena: A couple of gotchas — we sometimes have long prompts (500-1000 tokens) for docs summarization; TPOT matters then. Can measurement include those tails?
00:13:10 Ravi: Yes, we'll include prompt-length buckets: short (<64), medium (64-256), long (256-1024) and measure per-bucket TTFT/TPOT.

00:13:30 Marco: For sample prompts I'll annotate which are latency-sensitive vs batchable backrun jobs.

00:13:40 Maya: Great. Any objections to our proposed SLOs?
00:13:45 Lena: No objections, just want to see initial numbers quickly.
00:13:50 Marco: Agree.

00:14:05 Ravi: Quick note on measurement caveats: p99 is noisy — ensure long-enough runs and isolate network noise, use multiple runs and median-of-runs. We'll also provide raw timing so you can re-aggregate.
00:14:25 Priya: We'll run from a colo in us-west to minimize network noise.

00:14:40 Maya: Ok to recap next steps: Maya sends POC template/pricing and security docs; Ravi shares harness; Priya and Marco share histograms and prompts; schedule bench run week of 2026-04-06.

00:15:05 Ethan: Confirmed. One more Q — competitors? We're evaluating other vendors.
00:15:10 Lena: We are seeing Anthropic and Bespin in our shortlist.
00:15:15 Maya: We'll include comparison notes where helpful.

00:15:35 Marco: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

00:15:45 Maya: We'll follow up with calendar invite for bench kickoff and post the shared links in the CRM.

00:16:00 -- end of recorded highlights --

Notes on measurement plan (post-call):
- Use Redwood harness to capture token-level timings and backend timings; aggregate per-request TTFT and per-token intervals for TPOT.
- Ensure cache priming scripts run prior to warm tests (e.g., 10k warm requests).
- For cold-start TTFT, perform instance recycling between runs and include container startup time in measurement.
- Run three iterations per point and report median-of-runs for p95/p99 stability.
- Include resource telemetry (GPU utl, mem utilization) with each test to correlate latency spikes to scheduling or OOM events.
- Provide comparison table between model variants with quantization and batch settings.
